text:
maria (support): Hey team — customer ACME reported a sudden +2x spike on their March invoice vs dashboard. They say it happened after transient timeouts and client retries. invoice: INV-2026-1432, customer request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Can we triage? :eyes:

alex (billing): Thanks. Do we have example request/response headers or a trace id? Dashboard shows ~120k tokens, invoice charged ~240k.

maria (support): Customer pasted a curl sequence where their client retries on 504. They included this snippet:```POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Idempotency-Key: <missing>
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
... 
```They say their SDK didn't set an idempotency key.

lee (eng-runtime): If client doesn't send Idempotency-Key we dedupe only when we see the same external id? Our gateway generates ephemeral attempt ids. If a downstream ack arrives after timeout and the client replays, both can be counted unless internal dedupe matched. Need request traces.

sam (platform): tagging ingest-bot to pull raw ingress logs for req_0a1b2c3d window (around 2026-02-28T14:10Z). ingest-bot: queued.

ingest-bot: pulling logs from api-gateway-prod for 1987654320-1987654420, returning 6 ingress events for that client IP, 2 accepted, 4 timed out at gateway. Trace IDs: t-8f9e, t-8f9f, t-8fa0, t-8fa1, t-8fa2, t-8fa3.

alex (billing): Do our metering hooks run on accept only or on ingress? If we count on ingress we could double-charge on replay.

lee (eng-runtime): Metering fires when a request is persisted to ledger (post-accept). But we also emit interim usage on receive for dashboards (best-effort). Dashboard aggregates can be undercounted or overcounted depending on retries and replay order. Looks like the invoice ledger has two entries for the completed run and also a stale 'accept' event created by a late ack — need to inspect ledger rows.

maria (support): Customer says their client automatically retried at 1s and 3s after the initial request on network error. No idempotency header. They expect us to dedupe. They want refund for duplicate token usage.

lee (eng-runtime): Quick repro notes: simulate client with no Idempotency-Key doing TCP reset after request, then replay same payload. If gateway doesn't see the final ACK before client retries, both attempts can reach runtime and consume compute. We should verify whether the gateway sets X-Request-Receipt header that we use to collapse duplicates.

sam (platform): I pulled ledger rows: found two ledger entries with same payload hash and different internal_request_id (irid_7 and irid_9) but same customer_request_id absent. One created at 14:10:07, another at 14:10:11. Both charged. I'll open infra ticket to add supplemental dedupe by payload-hash+recent-window for missing idempotency-key flows.

alex (billing): From refund policy POV, we can issue a credit if we confirm duplicate charge within the same 30s replay window and identical token counts. Need engineering confirmation and a simple deterministic check.

lee (eng-runtime): I ran local sim and attached log excerpt:```[14:10:07.123] ingress: accept irid_7 payload-hash=0x5a3c tokens=1202
[14:10:08.456] runtime: start irid_7
[14:10:09.000] gateway: timeout client ACK not received
[14:10:11.200] ingress: accept irid_9 payload-hash=0x5a3c tokens=1202
[14:10:11.800] runtime: start irid_9
[14:10:12.900] runtime: complete irid_7
[14:10:13.500] runtime: complete irid_9
```This shows same payload processed twice.

maria (support): Customer asked for repro steps so they can patch their SDK. Can we produce recommended guidance?

lee (eng-runtime): Recommend always setting Idempotency-Key on mutating requests. Also implement client-side exponential backoff and only retry on idempotent-safe errors (e.g., 429, 5xx?). For immediate help, we can add a note in the dashboard explaining that retries without idempotency may be billed twice.

sam (platform): For this specific invoice I propose: 1) issue a credit for the duplicate entry once billing confirms ledger duplicate; 2) add an observability alert for >1 identical payload-hash processed within 10s for same customer; 3) prioritize a short-term gateway dedupe patch.

alex (billing): Agreed. I'll prepare credit memo draft pending a final ledger query. maria, please ask customer to confirm they will rotate any exposed keys and share any SDK logs.

maria (support): Sent: asked them for SDK logs and whether they rotated keys. Also offered provisional credit subject to engineering verification. They replied :thumbsup:.

billing-bot: created ticket BLG-5721 for credit request, amount: USD 1,223.40, linked invoice INV-2026-1432.

lee (eng-runtime): Follow-up: I added a quick ledger query to dedupe identical payload-hash within 15s window. Result: found the duplicate pair irid_7/irid_9 and marked irid_9 as candidate for credit. Patch PR when CI finishes.

sam (platform): CI green. Rolling hotfix to gateway dedupe for missing idempotency-key flows (short window 15s). Will monitor for false positives.

alex (billing): Once hotfix is verified, proceed with credit. Please attach ledger query and logs to BLG-5721.

maria (support): Will attach audit and close customer loop after credit applied. Thanks team! :raised_hands:
